<objective>
Fix the two parked Phase 01 defects inside the phase that already re-skins their files, each with its own
new regression test, and close both rows out in the Phase 01 UAT record.

Purpose: CONTEXT.md D-13 folds both defects into 01.1 rather than fixing them separately. The audit's own
argument is that they "live in the very components 01.1 re-skins — fixing them separately and then
re-skinning is duplicate work". One is a blocker: an owner cannot create a EUR venue at all, which makes
Phase 1's success criterion false as written. The other is a major: the venue switcher is stale
immediately after creation, and because the switcher renders nothing below two venues, on the
one-to-two transition the control **fails to appear at all** — on exactly the transition that creates the
need for it.

Output: two behavioural fixes, two new regression tests, and the UAT ledger reconciled.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID of its own. Closing the blocker unblocks
ACCT-03 on the **Phase 01** ledger; the bookkeeping task records that fact rather than claiming the
requirement for 01.1.

**Why this is the last code wave.** Putting the defect fixes first would make every later red ambiguous
between "the fix broke it" and "the re-skin broke it". Putting them last makes this plan's diff the only
suspect.

**How SC2 is read here.** SC2 requires the Phase 01 suite to pass *unchanged*. Both fixes move behaviour,
so the invariant is read as **"no existing test changes meaning", not "no test is added"** — D-13 states
this explicitly. Two tests are added; zero existing tests are edited.
</objective>

  <name>Task 1: G-01-13 — restore the last-enabled language to the submission without re-enabling the control</name>
  <files>components/venue-form.tsx, tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx</files>
  <read_first>
    - `components/venue-form.tsx` in full as left by plan 01.1-10 — the language checkbox block around lines 162-167 and the currency-change handler that seeds the enabled set
    - `lib/validation/venue.ts` — the per-currency defaults (the EUR default seeds a single language), the schema's minimum-length rule on the language array, and the language-code enum
    - `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` in full — it asserts the last-enabled checkbox is disabled, under an explicit rationale that the refusal should be visible rather than a dead click. That assertion must keep its meaning
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-RESEARCH.md` § "Pattern 5 — G-01-13: the EUR venue that cannot be created (D-13)" — the six-step mechanism traced end to end, the two rejected fixes and why, and the four assertions the new test must make
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-PATTERNS.md` § "`tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` (existing — the G-01-13 analog)" — the closest analog for the new DOM test
  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - With currency set to EUR: exactly one language checkbox is checked, and that checkbox is still rendered as disabled
    - With currency set to EUR: reading the enclosing form's data yields exactly one language entry, and its value is the English code — not merely non-empty, and not two entries
    - With currency set to RON (two seeded languages, nothing disabled): reading the form's data yields exactly two language entries, in the seeded order — proving the compensating input did not fire when it should not
    - The venue-creation schema parses the harvested form data successfully in the EUR case
  </behavior>
  <action>
    Write the failing test first. Assertion two is the one that fails today; assertion three is the one
    that fails if the fix is naive.

    **The mechanism, so the fix is not guessed.** The EUR currency default seeds the enabled-language set to
    a single entry. The form renders each language checkbox disabled when it is the only one left enabled,
    so the owner cannot accidentally remove their last language. Radix forwards that disabled flag to the
    hidden bubble input it uses to carry the value into form data — and HTML omits disabled controls from
    form submission. So for a EUR venue the only enabled language *was* the disabled one, the language array
    arrives empty, the schema's minimum-length rule rejects, and the error points at a checkbox the owner
    cannot tick. RON and HUF are unaffected because both seed two languages, so nothing is ever disabled.

    **Two fixes are wrong and must not be taken.** Re-enabling the checkbox and guarding on the server
    changes the meaning of an existing test, which asserts the disabled flag under a documented rationale —
    the refusal is meant to be visible rather than a dead click. That violates SC2 and the reasoning is
    sound. Marking the control read-only does not work either: the Radix checkbox has no such prop, and the
    corresponding ARIA attribute would not restore the value.

    **The fix.** Keep the control disabled, and render a sibling hidden input carrying the same field name
    and the same language code **only for the case where the control is both disabled and checked**. Guard
    it with the same predicate the disabled flag uses, so the compensating input never fires while the
    control is enabled. That guard is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the schema's array rule would tolerate a
    duplicate, but the database function would receive the language twice.

    Attach a comment block to the fix, following the repo's convention of naming the defect a guard exists
    for. It must record: the gap id; that the control stays disabled so the refusal stays visible; that
    Radix forwards the disabled flag to the hidden bubble input that carries the value, which HTML then
    omits; that the EUR default seeds exactly one language so the only enabled language was the disabled
    one; and that this restores the value without re-enabling the control.

    **Create `tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx`.** It needs a DOM, so give it a per-file jsdom
    directive — `vitest.config.ts` sets a node environment globally and the four existing `.tsx` tests each
    carry that directive. Follow `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` as the analog for rendering
    and querying. Assert all four `<behavior>` items. For the form-data assertions, read the enclosing form
    element and construct form data from it rather than simulating a submit, which is what makes the
    assertion about the browser's own omission rule rather than about a handler. Assert exact array
    equality, not length or non-emptiness.

    Open the file with a header block naming the defect class: a visibly-refused control whose value
    silently vanishes from the submission.

    **Do not edit `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx`.** If it goes red, the fix is wrong.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>pnpm exec vitest run tests/venues &amp;&amp; pnpm exec vitest run &amp;&amp; pnpm exec tsc --noEmit</automated>
  </verify>

    - `tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx` carries a per-file jsdom environment directive
    - The test asserts exact array equality for both the EUR case and the RON control case — `grep -cE 'toEqual\(\[' tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx` returns at least 2
    - The test calls the venue-creation schema's safe-parse on the harvested form data and asserts success
    - `grep -c 'type="hidden"' components/venue-form.tsx` returns 1

    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-PATTERNS.md` § "Revalidation after a mutation" — the exact import and call shape used by the sibling files
  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - The cache API is called exactly once on the success path, with both arguments pinned: the root path and the layout type
    - The call happens before the redirect — asserted by comparing the two mocks' invocation order, not by call count alone
    - The cache API is not called on any failure branch: no authenticated user, no account, or a database error
    - The redirect mock throws, as the real one does, so the test exercises the real control flow
  </behavior>
  <reversibility rating="reversible">Two defect fixes, each a few lines, each pinned by a regression test written to fail first. G-01-13 adds a hidden input alongside a disabled control and introduces no new server-side exposure — the value is re-validated by the language-code enum and the database CHECK constraint that already exist. G-01-14 adds one cache-purge call before an existing redirect. Neither changes a schema, a route or an authorization boundary, and task 3 only closes the two rows out in the Phase 01 UAT record. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Write the failing test first. Assertion two — the ordering — is the one that distinguishes a real fix
    from a cosmetic one; without it the test passes against a version that revalidates after the throw,
    which is to say never.

    **The mechanism.** The creation action ends by redirecting to the new venue and calls no cache API at
    all. The venue switcher is rendered by the dashboard layout, which is **shared** between the create
    route and the venue detail route, so on a soft navigation the framework reuses the cached shared-layout
    segment and the switcher shows the pre-creation list. For an owner creating their second venue this is
    worse than a stale name: the switcher renders nothing below two venues, so the control fails to appear
    at all on the one transition that creates the need for it.

    **The fix.** Import the cache-revalidation function from the framework's cache module and call it
    immediately before the redirect on the success path, with the root path and the layout type as its two
    arguments.

    Three details are load-bearing. **Placement:** the redirect signals by throwing, so anything after it
    never runs — the framework's own documentation states that revalidation calls belong before a redirect
    when the destination needs fresh data. **Both arguments:** calling with the path alone is a no-op for
    this defect and would pass a test that only counted calls, which is why the new test pins both.
    **Why the root plus the layout type:** the dashboard route group is invisible in the URL, so there is no
    path that *is* the dashboard layout; the framework documents that this argument pair purges the client
    cache and invalidates all cached data, and purging the client route cache is exactly and only what this
    defect needs, because the layout is already dynamic. The narrower alternative scoped to the venues path
    is defensible and has a smaller blast radius, but it is not obviously sufficient for a future sibling
    route outside that subtree that also renders the switcher.

    Do not reach for the newer tag-based read-your-own-writes API. This repo puts no cache tag on the venue
    read, the project conventions prescribe path revalidation, and introducing a tagging scheme is scope the
    phase does not need.

    Attach a comment block to the call recording the gap id, why the shared layout goes stale, why the
    missing-control case is worse than a stale label, why this argument pair, and that placement before the
    throwing redirect is mandatory.

    **Create `tests/actions/create-venue-revalidation.test.ts`** (node environment). Mock the framework's
    cache module and its navigation module, and make the redirect mock **throw**, as the real one does.
    Assert all four `<behavior>` items. For the ordering assertion, compare the two mocks' recorded
    invocation order rather than asserting on call counts.

    Open the file with a header block naming the defect class: a mutation that redirects into a shared
    layout without purging it, so the destination renders pre-mutation data.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>pnpm exec vitest run tests/actions &amp;&amp; pnpm exec vitest run &amp;&amp; pnpm exec tsc --noEmit &amp;&amp; pnpm build</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `pnpm exec vitest run tests/actions/create-venue-revalidation.test.ts` exits 0
    - `grep -c 'revalidatePath' actions/venues.ts` returns at least 2 — the import and the call
    - `grep -c 'revalidatePath("/", "layout")' actions/venues.ts` returns 1 — both arguments are pinned in source
    - In `actions/venues.ts`, the revalidation call appears on an earlier line than the redirect call: `test $(grep -n 'revalidatePath("/"' actions/venues.ts | cut -d: -f1) -lt $(grep -n 'redirect(' actions/venues.ts | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1)`
    - The test asserts ordering via `invocationCallOrder` — `grep -c 'invocationCallOrder' tests/actions/create-venue-revalidation.test.ts` returns at least 1
    - The test asserts the cache API is not called on at least three distinct failure branches
    - `pnpm exec vitest run tests/actions/venue-authority.test.ts` exits 0 (known timing-flaky; re-run once before treating a red there as real)
    - `pnpm exec vitest run` green at 464 + this phase's other additions; `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` exits 0; `pnpm build` exits 0
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>The client route cache is purged with both arguments pinned, before the throwing redirect, on the success path only — and the ordering is proven by call order rather than by call count.</done>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale. The ASVS V5 chapter named in the register below records that the input controls the G-01-13 fix relies on already exist and are unchanged — it is not a claim that this plan reviewed them.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| browser form → server action | The compensating hidden input adds a client-controllable value to the submitted language list. |
| server action → client route cache | The purge invalidates cached data for the redirect destination. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-06 | Tampering | Hidden-input value tampering introduced by the G-01-13 fix | low | accept | **No new exposure.** The value is re-validated server-side by the language-code enum — an exact-ASCII enum chosen precisely so no Unicode normalisation can smuggle a lookalike — and again by the database CHECK constraint on the supported-language column. The hidden input carries a value the enabled checkbox would have carried anyway. ASVS V5 is satisfied by controls that already exist. |
| T-01.1-45 | Tampering | A duplicate language value reaching the database function | medium | mitigate | The compensating input is guarded by the same predicate as the disabled flag, so it never fires while the control is enabled. The schema's array rule would tolerate a duplicate, so the guard is load-bearing; the RON control assertion in the new test is what catches a naive fix. |
| T-01.1-07 | Denial of Service | Over-broad cache purge on the root path | low | accept | The argument pair purges the **client** route cache only, and the dashboard layout is already dynamic, so no server-side cache entry is wastefully discarded. Negligible today; revisit if the diner ISR surface later shares a root. |
| T-01.1-46 | Repudiation | The UAT ledger rounded up to fully closed | medium | mitigate | The roll-up is unblocked on the currency leg only; the sign-in leg still needs a browser walk. The bookkeeping states that explicitly and a diff-size gate keeps the edit targeted rather than a rewrite. |
</threat_model>
